text: Sentinel: an autonomous options trading agent for the Alpaca A-I Trading Agents Hackathon. It trades unattended -- no human approves anything. Inside, the language model proposes, and deterministic gates decide.

An L-L-M trader's failure mode isn't being wrong. It's being confidently wrong -- at three times the size, in a symbol it invented. Most agents hand the model a broker tool. Sentinel gives it none. It proposes; the gates dispose.

Four pieces, one job each. The proposer ranks candidates and writes the thesis -- a brain, never a finger. Gates across five dimensions; an unregistered gate defaults to blocking. The permit is bound to the exact commit and policy hash, and expires in ninety minutes. And the executor accepts only a declared order shape -- none of them is a market order.

A quant engine first: regime, a per-name score, a gap detector. Four vectors consume it. Trend sells short-dated credit spreads with the regime -- eighty-seven percent wins over two hundred fifty simulated sessions. Catalyst is the Lululemon straddle; its drift leg measured negative over three years, so it's off. Event is the jobs report: a strangle, plus a zero-D-T-E gap continuation that won nine of ten. And Vol sells condors in a range. The model ranks. It never invents.

Every position is defined-risk -- no naked shorts, no market orders. Twelve thousand is the cap on one trade, always a fraction of starting equity, never of current. Forty thousand across the book, enforced at submission, not just declared. A kill switch at minus twelve thousand ends the day's entries. And below seventy thousand: no new exposure, but exits keep running.

On Alpaca: the Trading API for limit-only, multi-leg execution. Real-time I-E-X prices blended with the free options feed, delayed fifteen minutes -- so the snapshot's delta picks the strike, and Black-Scholes on the live underlying sets the price. M-C-P server and C-L-I both wired in.

And here's the live evidence. This dashboard reads a credential-free snapshot the agent writes every cycle -- no Alpaca keys in the hosted page. Before kickoff the market is closed, the market session gate is correctly red, the permit reads Blocked, and the agent sits in Entry Maintenance. A refused proposal, not a trusted claim.

This is a gate: plain code, a rationale, and a severity that can't quietly default to something weaker. And this is the permit -- bound to a commit and a policy hash, so one run can't borrow another's permission.
This is recorded before kickoff, so the results are deliberately blank. They come from account P-A-3-K-3-A-9-Z-B-C-B-I, reported whichever way they land.

Six scheduled catalysts sit inside this five-day window, and the agent never risks more than twelve percent on one idea. That's Sentinel. The repo and the live dashboard are on screen. Thanks for watching.
